newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds slip in lacklustre market.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds slip in lacklustre market.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished lower Tuesday as the market slipped on profit-taking in thin activity.
Traders said the market swung gently lower after the large gains last week, although trade was very thin amid what one trader said was a "boring market."
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 slipped $0.15 to 120.50, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 fell 1/8 to 84-3/4.
Market players said the underlying tone is still positive but in the absence of market-moving news, the market could drift in coming sessions.
"I do not think the market can rise much more now - I do not expect much fresh money will be heading towards the market before the beginning of next year," said an analyst at a large foreign bank.
The analyst added that he expected "a quiet week" ahead.

But the market remains supported by the increasing prospects of a strong rebound in growth. Abel Viglione, the chief economist at Argentina's FIEL consulting group, predicted Tuesday gross domestic product growth of 7.4 percent in the last quarter, topping the 6.6 percent provisional figure for the third quarter.
In the money markets, call money fell to 6.15 percent from 6.50 percent.
